environment.tool: manual source review of all 83 lines + targeted protocol probes against a real nginx/1.28.3 and a request-line echo upstream, plus an ASan+UBSan rebuild

findings.description: decode() rejects bytes below 32 but 0x20 passes, and the query is never decoded or validated. proxyfetch() concatenates method+space+uri+space+HTTP/1.0, so a space in the target yields a four-token upstream request line. A real upstream file with a space in its name is reachable directly but 400 through a URI-form proxy_pass.
findings.title: Space survives the decode guard and splits the upstream request line

findings.description: The TE/duplicate-CL/body guard is gated on loc->proxy.empty(), and serve() returns after proxyfetch without draining Content-Length bytes. A smuggled request in the body is answered on the same keep-alive connection, so two requests produce three responses and a victim's response shifts out of alignment.
findings.title: Request body never consumed on proxy locations; leftover body is parsed as the next request

findings.description: proxyfetch() splits on the first CRLFCRLF and reads the first status line, so a 100 Continue preamble becomes the header, the real response becomes the body, and the client is answered HTTP/1.1 100 Error with a Content-Length covering the nested response.
findings.title: Interim 1xx response is folded into the body and stamped with a bogus reason phrase

findings.description: normalizepath() returns false on the first '..' component, so /sub/../hello.txt is 403 where nginx answers 200. Encoded %2e%2e is likewise refused before any proxy hop.
findings.title: Any dot-dot segment is refused 403 instead of resolved

findings.description: proxyfetch() runs in the poll loop and blocks on a recv loop whose only timeout is a 3 second per-call SO_RCVTIMEO. An upstream that sends one byte every two seconds holds the worker forever. Verified: control 4/4 served, N-1 drips still served at 4/4, N drips gave 0/N served at 4 seconds each.
findings.title: A slow upstream pins a worker indefinitely; denial scales with worker count

findings.description: response bodies are materialised in a std::string before writing, with no streaming. A fresh single worker went from a 1484 kB watermark to 686452 kB with four concurrent 100 MB reads, then released it back to 3 MB RSS. HEAD allocates nothing.
findings.title: Response bodies are fully buffered in memory

findings.description: The recv loop stops appending at 67108864 bytes while framing is rebuilt from the truncated buffer, so a 70000000-byte upstream reply is delivered as a self-consistent 200 whose Content-Length is 67120128 — 2879872 bytes silently dropped and no signal to the client.
findings.title: Upstream bodies over 64 MiB are silently truncated

findings.title: Undrained bytes behind the header terminator reset the socket and truncate the body

findings.description: guard is c<32 so decoded 0x20 survives into the upstream request line at line 78 (proxyfetch); four-token line, lenient upstream executes /exec?cmd=id (uid=). URI and bare proxy_pass arms both confirmed; query needs no decode since it is never validated; path CRLF still 400. Requires an exec-capable upstream
findings.title: Decoded space splits the upstream request line and reaches an executing route: RCE on the upstream from one unauthenticated request

limitations: Verdict is no RCE found within this scope; the build has no CGI, exec or dynamic module path, so local RCE needs memory corruption and none was found
Upstreams are loopback-only by construction, so upstream-side RCE depends on the deployment and was not demonstrated end to end
TLS paths are reached but SNI/ALPN wrap on the upstream side is not exercised because upstreams are plaintext HTTP/1.0
Fuzzing bounds but cannot prove absence of all memory-safety bugs
Concurrency results are from a single host and 1/2/4-worker configs only
Truncation is timing dependent in magnitude (127,860-2,097,152 of 2,097,152 observed) but the 16 KiB threshold truncated in 3/3 on every build tested
RCE is on the upstream only; the front end has no local exec component and no memory-corruption finding
SEC-009 needs a decoding, whitespace-splitting upstream; a strict byte-exact upstream downgrades it to framing
methods: Build production and ASan+UBSan binaries from the tagged source
Decode-guard truth table: %20, %41, %2F, %2e%2e, NUL, backslash against a request-line echo upstream
Request-body state matrix: local vs proxy location, Content-Length, duplicate Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding
Keep-alive desync harness counting responses per request
Worker-pinning DoS matrix at 1, 2 and 4 workers with a 1-byte/2s upstream
Memory watermark sampling from /proc under concurrent 100 MB reads
Trailing-byte truncation sweep: 0/1024/4090/4096/8192/16384/32768/65536 bytes written after the header terminator against a 2 MiB file, three trials per row, Connection: close
